q: A program is a ______ entity, while a process is an ______ entity.
explain: **Program = passive entity** (ملف على الديسك)، و **Process = active entity** (شغالة في الميموري).

q: A program becomes a process when:
choices: It is saved on the disk
Its executable file is loaded into memory
explain: **A program becomes a process when an executable file is loaded into the memory**.

q: The fundamental task of any operating system is:
explain: **The fundamental task of any operating system is the process management**.

q: Besides the program text, a process includes:
choices: Resources such as open files and pending signals, processor state, address space, and a data section
explain: الـ process فيها كمان **set of resources** زي open files و pending signals، و internal kernel data، و processor state، و address space، و data section.

q: Which is NOT a responsibility of the OS toward processes?
choices: Writing the source code of processes
explain: الـ OS لازم: **allocate resources**, **enable sharing**, **protect resources**, **enable synchronization**. لكن مبيكتبش كود البرامج.

q: Global variables of a process are stored in the:
explain: **Data Section: containing global variables**.

q: Function parameters, return addresses and local variables are stored in the:
explain: **Stack: temporary data** (function parameters, return addresses, local variables).

q: Memory dynamically allocated during run time is in the:
explain: **Heap: memory dynamically allocated during run time** (زي malloc).

q: The program code of a process is stored in the:
explain: **Text Section: the program code**.

q: Which process segment is typically read-only and might be shared by a number of processes?
explain: الـ **Text section** غالبًا **read-only** وممكن كذا process يشتركوا فيه (نفس البرنامج مفتوح أكتر من مرة).

q: In the 'process in memory' layout, which segment is at the highest address (max) and grows downward?
explain: الترتيب من max لـ 0: **stack** ← (free) ← heap ← data ← text. الـ **stack** فوق وبيكبر لتحت، والـ heap بيكبر لفوق.

q: Each process is represented in the OS by a:
explain: **Each process is represented in the OS by a Process Control Block (PCB)**.

q: The program counter in the PCB holds:
choices: The location of the next instruction to execute
explain: **Program counter = location of instruction to next execute**.

q: Priorities and scheduling queue pointers are part of which PCB information?
explain: **CPU scheduling information: priorities, scheduling queue pointers**.

q: CPU used, clock time elapsed since start, and time limits are part of:
explain: **Accounting information: CPU used, clock time elapsed since start, time limits**.

q: I/O devices allocated to a process and its list of open files are stored in:
explain: **I/O status information: I/O devices allocated to process, list of open files**.

q: Process identification information in the PCB includes all of the following EXCEPT:
explain: الـ **Process identification**: process ID، و user ID، و parent process ID. أما الـ **CPU registers** فجزء تاني من الـ PCB.

q: The process state (running, waiting, etc.) belongs to which PCB category?
explain: **Processor state Information: Process state – running, waiting, etc**.

q: Memory allocated to the process is recorded in:
explain: **Memory-management information: memory allocated to the process**.

q: A process that is being created is in the ______ state.
explain: **new: The process is being created**.

q: A process waiting to be assigned to a processor is in the ______ state.
explain: **ready: The process is waiting to be assigned to a processor**. أما **waiting** فمستنية حدث (event) زي I/O.

q: A process waiting for some event (such as I/O completion) to occur is in the ______ state.
explain: **waiting: The process is waiting for some event to occur**.

q: A process whose instructions are being executed is in the ______ state.
explain: **running: Instructions are being executed**.

q: Which transition moves a process from ready to running?
explain: **ready → running = scheduler dispatch**: الـ scheduler اختارها.

q: When an interrupt occurs, a running process moves to the:
explain: **running → ready (interrupt)**: الـ process بتتقاطع وترجع تستنى دورها.

q: When a running process requests I/O, it moves to the:
explain: **running → waiting (I/O or event wait)**.

q: After its I/O completes, a waiting process moves to the:
explain: **waiting → ready (I/O or event completion)**. مش بتروح running على طول، لازم تستنى الـ scheduler.

q: The transition from new to ready is called:
explain: **new → ready = admitted**.

q: Which transition does NOT exist in the process state diagram?
explain: **مفيش waiting → running مباشرة**. الـ process بعد ما الحدث يحصل بتروح **ready** الأول.

q: On a single processor, how many processes can be in the running state at any instant?
choices: As many as in the ready queue
explain: على كل processor فيه **process واحدة بس running** في أي لحظة، والباقيين ready أو waiting.

q: When the CPU switches from process P0 to process P1, the OS must:
choices: Reload the state from PCB0 only
Save the state into PCB0 and reload the state from PCB1
explain: الـ **context switch**: **save state into PCB0** وبعدين **reload state from PCB1**.

q: Which statement about the context switch is TRUE?
choices: It happens only at boot time
It is overhead; the system does no useful work while switching
explain: الـ context switch **overhead**: النظام مبيعملش شغل مفيد وقته، وعشان كده لازم يبقى سريع.

q: The set of ALL processes in the system is the:
explain: **Job queue – set of all processes in the system**.

q: The set of all processes residing in main memory, ready and waiting to execute, is the:
explain: **Ready queue – set of all processes residing in main memory, ready and waiting to execute**.

q: Processes waiting for an I/O device are kept in the:
explain: **Device queues – set of processes waiting for an I/O device**.

q: In the queueing diagram, when a process's time slice expires, it goes back to the:
explain: **time slice expired** ← ترجع **ready queue** على طول.

q: Which event in the queueing diagram creates a new process?
explain: **fork a child**: الـ process بتعمل child، والـ child بيتنفذ، وبعدين ترجع للـ ready queue.

q: The short-term scheduler is also called the:
explain: **Short-term scheduler (or CPU scheduler)**.

q: The long-term scheduler is also called the:
explain: **Long-term scheduler (or job scheduler)**.

q: Which scheduler selects which process should be executed next and allocates the CPU?
explain: الـ **Short-term (CPU) scheduler** بيختار الـ process الجاية ويدّيها الـ CPU.

q: Which scheduler is invoked very frequently (milliseconds) and therefore must be fast?
explain: **Short-term: invoked frequently (milliseconds) → must be fast**.

q: Which scheduler controls the degree of multiprogramming?
explain: **Long-term scheduler: controls the degree of multiprogramming**، وبيشتغل infrequently (seconds, minutes) فممكن يبقى بطيء.

q: The long-term scheduler selects which processes should be brought into the:
explain: الـ **Long-term** بيختار **which processes should be brought into the ready queue**.

q: Removing a process from memory, storing it on disk, and bringing it back later to continue execution is called:
explain: ده **swapping** وبيعمله الـ **medium-term scheduler**.

q: The medium-term scheduler can be added when the degree of multiprogramming needs to:
explain: **Medium-term scheduler: can be added if degree of multiple programming needs to decrease**.

q: Cooperating processes need:
explain: **Cooperating processes need interprocess communication (IPC)**.

q: A process that can affect or be affected by other processes, including sharing data, is a(n):
explain: **Cooperating process can affect or be affected by other processes, including sharing data**. أما الـ independent فمبتأثرش ولا بتتأثر.

q: The two models of IPC are:
explain: **Two models of IPC: Shared memory · Message passing**.

q: In which IPC model do processes exchange messages through a message queue maintained by the kernel?
explain: في الـ **message passing** الرسايل (m0, m1, ..., mn) بتعدي على **message queue في الـ kernel**. أما الـ shared memory فالـ processes بتقرا وتكتب في منطقة مشتركة.

q: Which IPC model is generally faster because the kernel is involved only when establishing the shared region?
explain: الـ **Shared memory** أسرع، لأن الـ kernel بيتدخل بس وقت إنشاء المنطقة. أما الـ message passing فمحتاج system call لكل رسالة.
